wrong_picks.title: EgoPlan-Bench: where wrong picks fall
wrong_picks.takeaway: All three models, when wrong, pick a step just ahead.

cases.alt: Three frames of a robot arm at a table with a bowl, a cup and a spoon; the question asks which sub-task comes next. Ours answers “Pick up the spoon” (score 100); Astra and Opus score 0.
cases.why: The gripper is empty and the spoon still lies on the table. Both closed models continue from a state that has not been reached: one scoops with a spoon that is not held, and the other pours without scooping at all.

cases.alt: Four frames of a robot ironing a garment; the question asks which sub-task comes next. Ours picks option B, the reference; Astra and Opus pick option A.
cases.why: Opus observes correctly that the left arm has released the garment, yet concludes that ironing goes on. The release marks the end of the ironing sub-goal, and what remains is to put the iron back into its slot on the stand.

cases.alt: Four frames of a gripper above a red and a green cube; the question asks in which phase the error happened. Ours picks option B, the reference; Astra and Opus pick option C.
cases.why: The red cube never leaves the table: the error happened while the gripper was reaching for it. Both closed models name the phase in which the consequence shows (nothing is lifted), one step after the phase that caused it.

cases.alt: Two frames of a robot gripper near an open cabinet; the question asks whether the move-to step is finished. Ours answers No, the reference; Astra and Opus answer Yes.
cases.why: The gripper has moved but is still at the top of the cabinet, away from the open door. Both closed models take motion toward the target for arrival; a step is complete when its end state is reached, not when motion is made.
